transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just felt really low for a long time. Like, not just a bad day or a rough week. It’s been going on for the last couple of years, and it’s kind of always there in the background.

Even when I’m at work, or at church, or around people I really do care about, I still feel this heavy, empty feeling. It doesn’t really lift. I can be sitting there with everyone and still feel like I’m carrying this weight inside me, and I don’t really know how to make it stop.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean… I still do some of the same things I used to do, but I don’t always know if I’d call it “pleasure” the way I used to.

Like, I can go through the motions of things, and sometimes I’ll have moments where I’m distracted or it’s okay, but it’s hard for me to tell if I’m actually enjoying it or just doing it because it’s familiar, or because I’m supposed to, or because people expect me to show up. I don’t know. It’s not like I never smile or anything, but it feels complicated when you ask it that directly.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to like?

I don’t know if I’d say I’ve completely lost interest… it’s more like everything feels dulled down. Like, I still know what I used to like, and sometimes I still try to do those things, but the feeling doesn’t really show up the same way.

It’s hard to explain because if someone asked me, “Do you like this?” I’d probably say yes, because in my head I know I do—or I used to. But actually wanting to do it, looking forward to it, feeling excited about it… that part feels kind of distant. Sometimes I’ll go along with something and think, maybe once I’m there it’ll feel better, but a lot of the time I’m just sort of present, not really into it.

So… yeah, maybe some interest is gone, or maybe it’s just buried under how I’ve been feeling. I’m not totally sure.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or ending your life?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I know what you’re asking, and it’s kind of a scary question to hear out loud.

I haven’t really… I don’t have a clear thing to tell you, like a specific plan or something. It’s more like sometimes when I’m feeling really weighed down, I get tired of feeling that way, and I don’t know what to do with it. But I’m not sure if that counts as what you mean.

I guess I’d say I haven’t been walking around with some detailed intention to hurt myself, but the question makes me nervous because the feelings can get really heavy. I’m sorry, I’m probably not explaining it very well.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling that you mentioned?

It’s been… a little over two years, I think. About two years and four months, if I’m counting it right.

It started around when I had to stop taking my community-college classes. I couldn’t really make it work anymore because of money and my work schedule, and after that it was like this heaviness just kind of settled in. At first I thought maybe I was just disappointed or stressed and it would pass once I adjusted, but it didn’t really lift. It’s hard to separate the exact day or anything, because it wasn’t like one morning I woke up and everything was suddenly different. It was more gradual, but that’s the point I keep coming back to—when I had to stop school. Since then, it’s pretty much been there in some form.
Do you often feel nervous or anxious, even when there's no apparent reason to feel that way?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I do get nervous sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s often or for no reason. Usually I can kind of point to something, even if it’s small or probably not that big of a deal—like work stuff, or feeling like I’m behind, or worrying I said something weird. But I don’t know if that’s the kind of anxiety you mean.

It’s hard because sometimes the nervous feeling is just sort of mixed in with everything else, so I don’t always notice it as “anxiety,” exactly. I’ll just feel tense or unsettled and then later I’ll realize I’ve been worrying in the background. But I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean like sudden panic or being anxious all the time for no clear reason. I don’t think I’ve noticed it that clearly.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past two years?

Yeah… I think so. I haven’t been tracking it carefully, like I’m not weighing myself every week or anything, but I’ve definitely noticed my clothes fitting differently. My work pants especially—some months they feel tighter, and then other times they’re loose enough that I notice it when I’m moving around at work.

It kind of goes along with how I’m eating, I guess. A lot of days I just don’t eat much during my shift because nothing sounds good, or I keep telling myself I’ll eat later and then suddenly the shift is almost over. And then other days, when I’m really drained, I’ll end up getting vending machine stuff late, not because I’m actually hungry in a normal way, but just because it’s there and I’m tired and I don’t have the energy to think about real food.

So, yeah, it’s been up and down. I don’t know the exact number, but enough that I’ve noticed it.
Have you noticed any changes in how active or energetic you are compared to how you used to be?

Yeah, definitely. I feel like I have way less energy than I used to, and it’s not even just for big things. It’s small, normal stuff that shouldn’t feel like a whole task.

Like at work, even filling out the inspection logs can feel like I’m dragging myself through it. It’s not hard exactly, I know how to do it, but it feels like it takes so much focus and energy just to sit there and get it done. And outside of work, even driving to basketball—something I used to do without thinking—can feel like this big ordeal, like I’m already tired before I even leave.

Even washing my hair feels like too much sometimes. I’ll know I need to do it, and I’ll keep putting it off because standing there and going through all the steps just feels like more than I have in me. And then on my days off, I’ll think, okay, I’ll rest and then I’ll feel better, but it doesn’t really work that way. I can sleep in or lie around and still feel like I didn’t refill at all. It’s like my battery just doesn’t charge the way it used to.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to end your life in the past few months?

I… I’m not really sure how to answer that clearly. I don’t think I have a specific answer I can give you. Like, I know you’re asking about wanting to end my life, and that feels like a really serious thing to say yes or no to, so I don’t want to answer wrong or make it sound more definite than it is.

I guess what I can say is… I haven’t really sorted it out in my head enough to give you a clean answer. Sometimes when things are bad, my thoughts get kind of heavy and everything feels like too much, but I don’t know if that’s the same as actually wanting to end my life. I’m trying to think about the past few months specifically, and it’s just… hard to separate out. So I guess I’d say I’m not sure.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the way you mean, I guess.

Like, I’ve never seen a person standing there who wasn’t actually there, or heard a voice talking to me when nobody was around. Sometimes I’ll think I hear my name or a sound at work, but usually that’s just the machines or people moving around, and when I check, there’s some normal explanation or it just kind of goes away. I don’t really have anything where I’m convinced I’m seeing or hearing something other people can’t.

So… no, I don’t think that’s been happening.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you didn't feel this low?

No… I don’t think I’ve had a stretch that long where I really felt okay or not low. It’s been pretty constant.

I’d say this has been going on for about two years and… maybe four months now. It started around when I had to stop taking community college classes, because I couldn’t really make it work with money and my work schedule. I kept thinking maybe once I adjusted, or once work settled down, I’d feel more like myself again, but it just kind of stayed there.

There might be individual days where I’m a little less down, or I can distract myself for a while, but not like a full two months where I’d say I wasn’t feeling this way. Not really.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed anything really obvious like… people telling me I’m talking too slowly, or that I’m pacing around all the time or something.

Sometimes I feel like it takes me longer to answer people, like my brain has to kind of push through mud before I can say what I mean, but I don’t know if that’s the same as actually speaking slower. And at work I’m usually trying to keep up with what I’m supposed to be doing, so I don’t really pay attention to how I’m moving unless someone points it out, which I don’t think they have.

Restless… maybe sometimes I shift around or can’t get comfortable, but I wouldn’t say I’m unable to sit still in a noticeable way. So I guess my answer is I haven’t really noticed either one clearly.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s not like I can’t ever laugh at something or have one okay moment, but the things that used to actually make me feel happy or excited just don’t really do that anymore.

Like basketball used to be a big thing for me. Dance nights too. And I was doing this church STEM mentoring thing that I actually cared about — like, I liked showing up and helping, and it felt like it mattered. But I’ve mostly stopped going to all of that. It’s not even always because I’m busy. Sometimes I just… can’t make myself go, or I think about going and it feels like too much, and also kind of pointless, even though I know I used to enjoy it.

And it’s affecting work too. I’ve gotten written warnings because I’ve been missing shifts and turning in my inspection documentation late. I know that’s not exactly “pleasure,” but it’s like the same thing is spilling over everywhere — I’m not engaged, I’m not looking forward to anything, and even stuff I used to care about feels far away from me now.
Do you find that your low mood stays with you all day, or are there times during the day when you feel a little better?

It’s… honestly kind of with me most of the day. I don’t think it really lifts in a clean way, like where I can say, “Oh, I felt normal for the afternoon.” It’s more like it changes volume, if that makes sense.

Like sometimes if I’m at work and I’m focused on what I’m supposed to be checking or sorting, I can get through the task and not be thinking about it every second, but it’s still there underneath. Same if I’m at church or around people I care about — I might talk, I might smile a little, I might even have a moment where I’m distracted — but there’s still this heavy, empty feeling sitting there. It doesn’t really go away.

I think that’s part of why I’m here, because it’s been like that for the last couple years. Not just a bad morning or a bad night. It’s like I wake up with it, carry it around, and even if parts of the day are a little less intense, I don’t really feel free from it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two years?

Not like one big dramatic weight loss that I can point to, I don’t think. It’s more… my eating has been really inconsistent, and my weight kind of goes up and down.

Most days I either don’t eat much at all until my shift is almost over, because nothing sounds good or I just don’t feel like dealing with food, and then by the end I’m so drained that I’ll grab something from the vending machine — chips, candy, whatever’s easy — not because I really want it, just because I realize I haven’t eaten. So it’s not exactly a normal appetite.

I’ve noticed it mostly because my work pants fit different from month to month. Sometimes they feel looser, then later they’re tight again, and I’m like… okay, clearly something is changing, but I haven’t been tracking the number closely. So I wouldn’t say I know I lost a significant amount over two years, but there’s definitely been weight and appetite changes.
Do you find that your low mood is worse at any particular time of day?

I don’t know that there’s one specific time where I can say, like, “it’s always worst at 6 p.m.” or something. It’s more that it’s just… there most of the time, and it kind of changes shape depending on what I’m doing.

Like mornings can be hard because I wake up and it’s already there, that heavy feeling, before anything has even happened. But then at work, even if I’m busy inspecting or sorting or trying to stay on task, it doesn’t really leave — it’s just sort of pushed to the background. And then if I’m at church or around people I care about, I can still talk and act mostly normal for a little bit, but underneath I still feel low and empty.

So I guess the best way to say it is, it’s not really tied to a time of day for me. It’s been like this for the last couple years, where I just feel low all the time, and even when I’m somewhere that should help or with people who matter to me, it doesn’t really lift.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled by someone or something else?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where my thoughts feel really loud or hard to get away from, like I get stuck in my own head, but not like someone else is controlling them.

I don’t feel like there’s a person or a force putting thoughts in my mind or making me think things. It’s more just… my own thoughts can feel heavy and repetitive, if that makes sense. But they still feel like mine.
Is there any pattern to when your low mood feels the worst during the day?

I don’t think there’s a clear daily pattern, honestly. It’s not like I wake up and it’s only bad in the morning, or it always crashes at night. It’s more that for the last couple years I just feel low all the time, like it’s sitting there underneath everything.

Even when I’m at work and I’m trying to focus, or when I’m at church, or around people I care about, it doesn’t really lift. I might be distracted for a while or seem normal from the outside, but inside there’s still this heavy, empty feeling. So I guess I’d say it’s not really tied to a certain time of day — it’s just kind of always there.
Is your low mood usually worse in the mornings, afternoons, or evenings, or does it vary from day to day?

It varies, I guess, but not even in a way where I can point to mornings or afternoons or evenings as the problem. It’s more like… it’s just there all the time. Like I’m here because for the last couple years I’ve felt low pretty much constantly, and it doesn’t really seem to depend on the time of day.

I can be at work, trying to focus on what I’m supposed to be doing, or at church, or even around people I really care about, and there’s still this heavy, empty feeling underneath everything. Sometimes I’m distracted from it for a little while, so maybe it feels less obvious, but it doesn’t actually lift. So I wouldn’t say mornings or evenings are consistently worse. It’s more just always there, and some days I notice it more than others.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your friends and family?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean… I worry sometimes that people are tired of dealing with me, or that I’m not as easy to be around as I should be, but I don’t know if I’d say I constantly feel like a burden in a clear way.

It’s more like I second-guess myself. Like if I’m quiet, or not really able to act normal, I start thinking maybe I’m bringing the mood down or making things harder for people. But I don’t always know if that’s actually true or just me reading into things. So… I guess sometimes I feel that way, but it’s not something I’ve really talked through or put into words much.

target_item.reason: The question is about psychomotor changes, such as moving or speaking more slowly than usual or feeling restless and unable to sit still, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed anything really obvious like… people telling me I’m talking too slowly, or that I’m pacing around all the time or something.

Sometimes I feel like it takes me longer to answer people, like my brain has to kind of push through mud before I can say what I mean, but I don’t know if that’s the same as actually speaking slower. And at work I’m usually trying to keep up with what I’m supposed to be doing, so I don’t really pay attention to how I’m moving unless someone points it out, which I don’t think they have.

Restless… maybe sometimes I shift around or can’t get comfortable, but I wouldn’t say I’m unable to sit still in a noticeable way. So I guess my answer is I haven’t really noticed either one clearly.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve gotten written warnings at work because I’m missing shifts and turning in inspection documentation late, and I’ve mostly stopped showing up for basketball, dance nights, and the church STEM mentoring I used to care about.
target_item.reason: The question asks about loss of pleasure or interest in normally enjoyable activities. The profile does not include a specific anhedonia item, but the functional impairment item directly mentions mostly stopping activities previously cared about, like basketball, dance nights, and church STEM mentoring.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s not like I can’t ever laugh at something or have one okay moment, but the things that used to actually make me feel happy or excited just don’t really do that anymore.

Like basketball used to be a big thing for me. Dance nights too. And I was doing this church STEM mentoring thing that I actually cared about — like, I liked showing up and helping, and it felt like it mattered. But I’ve mostly stopped going to all of that. It’s not even always because I’m busy. Sometimes I just… can’t make myself go, or I think about going and it feels like too much, and also kind of pointless, even though I know I used to enjoy it.

And it’s affecting work too. I’ve gotten written warnings because I’ve been missing shifts and turning in my inspection documentation late. I know that’s not exactly “pleasure,” but it’s like the same thing is spilling over everywhere — I’m not engaged, I’m not looking forward to anything, and even stuff I used to care about feels far away from me now.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's low mood is consistently present throughout the day
doctor.question: Do you find that your low mood stays with you all day, or are there times during the day when you feel a little better?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for the last couple years I just feel low all the time, like even when I’m at work or church or around people I care about, there’s this heavy empty feeling that doesn’t really lift.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the persistence and daily pattern of the patient’s low mood, which directly matches the depressed mood symptom.

patient.answer:
It’s… honestly kind of with me most of the day. I don’t think it really lifts in a clean way, like where I can say, “Oh, I felt normal for the afternoon.” It’s more like it changes volume, if that makes sense.

Like sometimes if I’m at work and I’m focused on what I’m supposed to be checking or sorting, I can get through the task and not be thinking about it every second, but it’s still there underneath. Same if I’m at church or around people I care about — I might talk, I might smile a little, I might even have a moment where I’m distracted — but there’s still this heavy, empty feeling sitting there. It doesn’t really go away.

I think that’s part of why I’m here, because it’s been like that for the last couple years. Not just a bad morning or a bad night. It’s like I wake up with it, carry it around, and even if parts of the day are a little less intense, I don’t really feel free from it.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant weight loss
doctor.question: Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two years?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Most days I either skip eating until my shift is almost over because nothing sounds good, or I end up grabbing vending machine snacks late just because I’m drained, and my weight has been up and down enough that my work pants fit different from month to month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking directly about significant weight change over the past two years.

patient.answer:
Not like one big dramatic weight loss that I can point to, I don’t think. It’s more… my eating has been really inconsistent, and my weight kind of goes up and down.

Most days I either don’t eat much at all until my shift is almost over, because nothing sounds good or I just don’t feel like dealing with food, and then by the end I’m so drained that I’ll grab something from the vending machine — chips, candy, whatever’s easy — not because I really want it, just because I realize I haven’t eaten. So it’s not exactly a normal appetite.

I’ve noticed it mostly because my work pants fit different from month to month. Sometimes they feel looser, then later they’re tight again, and I’m like… okay, clearly something is changing, but I haven’t been tracking the number closely. So I wouldn’t say I know I lost a significant amount over two years, but there’s definitely been weight and appetite changes.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's low mood is worse at a specific time of day
doctor.question: Do you find that your low mood is worse at any particular time of day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for the last couple years I just feel low all the time, like even when I’m at work or church or around people I care about, there’s this heavy empty feeling that doesn’t really lift.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the daily pattern and timing of the patient's low mood, which directly relates to the persistent depressed mood symptom.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that there’s one specific time where I can say, like, “it’s always worst at 6 p.m.” or something. It’s more that it’s just… there most of the time, and it kind of changes shape depending on what I’m doing.

Like mornings can be hard because I wake up and it’s already there, that heavy feeling, before anything has even happened. But then at work, even if I’m busy inspecting or sorting or trying to stay on task, it doesn’t really leave — it’s just sort of pushed to the background. And then if I’m at church or around people I care about, I can still talk and act mostly normal for a little bit, but underneath I still feel low and empty.

So I guess the best way to say it is, it’s not really tied to a time of day for me. It’s been like this for the last couple years, where I just feel low all the time, and even when I’m somewhere that should help or with people who matter to me, it doesn’t really lift.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about experiences of thought control or passivity, which are psychotic symptoms; this is not covered by the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where my thoughts feel really loud or hard to get away from, like I get stuck in my own head, but not like someone else is controlling them.

I don’t feel like there’s a person or a force putting thoughts in my mind or making me think things. It’s more just… my own thoughts can feel heavy and repetitive, if that makes sense. But they still feel like mine.

It varies, I guess, but not even in a way where I can point to mornings or afternoons or evenings as the problem. It’s more like… it’s just there all the time. doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're a burden to your friends and family?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about feelings of being a burden, which relates to worthlessness or excessive guilt; that symptom is not included in the provided profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean… I worry sometimes that people are tired of dealing with me, or that I’m not as easy to be around as I should be, but I don’t know if I’d say I constantly feel like a burden in a clear way.

It’s more like I second-guess myself. Like if I’m quiet, or not really able to act normal, I start thinking maybe I’m bringing the mood down or making things harder for people. But I don’t always know if that’s actually true or just me reading into things. So… I guess sometimes I feel that way, but it’s not something I’ve really talked through or put into words much.
